english.title: Owner / occupier fail to comply with management notice
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the

(A)_[owner]_
(B)_[occupier]_

of land falling within a site of special scientific interest, and being subject to a management notice served under section 28K of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981, failed, without reasonable excuse, to comply with the requirements of that notice, namely **(..SPECIFY REQUIREMENT(S)..), within the time allowed
english.legislation: Contrary to section 28P(8) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See Section 28K for "management notice".
(ii) As inserted by paragraph 1 of Schedule 9 to the Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000.
(iii) Section 28P(10) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 provides that proceedings in England and Wales for an offence under Section 28P shall not, without the consent of the DPP, be taken by a person other than English Nature or the Natural Resources Body for Wales.

(A)_[berchennog]_
(B)_[feddiannwr]_

tir sydd o fewn safle o ddiddordeb gwyddonol arbennig, a bu i chi yn destun hysbysiad rheoli a gyflwynwyd dan adran 28K Deddf Bywyd Gwyllt a Chefn Gwlad 1981, fethu, heb esgus rhesymol, i gydymffurfio â gofynion yr hysbysiad hwnnw, sef **(..SPECIFY REQUIREMENT(S)..), o fewn yr amser a ganiatawyd

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: A fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
